title: Mongol Empire
capsule: United under Chinggis Khan's proclamation as universal khan at a 1206 kurultai, the Mongol Empire (Yeke Mongghol Ulus, the 'Great Mongol State') expanded within two generations into history's largest contiguous land empire, conquering the Khwarazmian Empire, the Jin and Western Xia states, Rus', and much of the Islamic Middle East under Chinggis's successors Ögedei, Güyük and Möngke. Möngke's death in 1259 triggered the Toluid Civil War between his brothers Kublai and Ariq Böke, after which the empire fractured into autonomous khanates — the Yuan dynasty in China, the Ilkhanate in Persia, the Chagatai Khanate in Central Asia, and the Golden Horde in the Pontic-Caspian steppe. By Kublai Khan's death in 1294, the once-unified empire persisted only as a loose, largely ceremonial confederation of these separate Chinggisid states.
